title: RCMP's sour relationship contributed to shooting: chief
article: The chief of Norway House First Nation says his community's relationship with the RCMP had deteriorated in the months before Monday's shooting in the community, and may have contributed to the tragedy.

Dennis St. Paul was finishing his shift as a dishwasher at a local restaurant on Monday when an RCMP constable tried to arrest him for parole violations. RCMP say the two men struggled after a foot chase, and two shots were fired. St. Paul, 30, died later in hospital.
Norway House Chief Ron Evans says his community's problems with the RCMP go back to August 2004, when a new sergeant arrived.
Evans says the sergeant was difficult to work with, and alienated not only his community, but also his junior staff. Those officers began leaving Norway House.
After complains from Evans and other community members, the sergeant was transferred, but he wasn't replaced. That left Norway House with a new police team, but no senior officer.

"There was a whole new turnover of new members that came into Norway House. That's a recipe for disaster," says Evans. "In the meantime, there was no mature, experienced person to oversee this recruitment of young RCMP officers. Had that been the case, perhaps the incident that happened in our community the other day a mature, experienced person could have prevented that."
RCMP will not confirm Evans version of events. However, the chief has been told a sergeant who used to work in Norway House will arrive shortly - one with a good reputation in the community.
"He's just a wonderful human being that's going to go a long way in terms of moving in the direction we need to," says Evans.
The sergeant will fill in until a permanent replacement can be found.
